_extract.note: Complete reverse-audit extract for the LaunchDarkly six-pack suite. It admits all official method/path operations except two multipart CSV uploads that the current REST binding cannot represent safely.
_extract.unpaged_collection_note: These array-shaped reads have no supported continuation contract in the pinned OpenAPI. They remain one-dispatch calls and are not marked single_page, so the runtime does not certify completeness without evidence.

semantic_patch_variant.reason: Preserves the documented semantic patch variant used by the bundled turnFlagOn and turnFlagOff workflows.

transport_notes.context_search: The two context-search POST routes select their documented query-parameter alternative. LaunchDarkly rejects calls that mix query and request-body modes; choosing query mode also retains includeTotalCount.
transport_notes.multipart: The two CSV-only multipart routes remain explicitly excluded until file_ref request-body support exists.

exclusions.reason: An SDK key IS a credential — LaunchDarkly's own schema says of the `value` field: "The string value of the SDK key. Use this when configuring your SDK." These reads returned it in an ordinary operation result at risk `read` with approval `never`, so any recipe that could list SDK keys could also read, log and forward them with nothing asked. Ordinary operation results are not a secret result channel. Creating, rotating and deleting SDK keys remain available and approval-gated; only the paths that hand back the secret itself are closed.
